entries.comment: Reviewed at main 7ff2e5d1ced33065f40cfd0d1151635c18a9e0b1. The printf call reports the native zoom test's DPI as an integer. This fixture is compiled on the supported Linux/GCC 13 baseline: .github/actions/dependencies/action.yml installs gcc-13/g++-13 and exports CC=gcc-13 and CXX=g++-13. GCC's libstdc++ implementation table lists P2093R14 formatted output (std::print/std::println and <print>) as first supported in GCC 14.1, and the GCC 14 release notes identify these as additions. Replacing this call with the suggested std::print would fail to compile on the project's supported compiler. Retain the existing typed printf arguments and diagnostics. References: https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/libstdc++/manual/status.html and https://gcc.gnu.org/gcc-14/changes.html . This disposition applies to this std::print recommendation; std::format recommendations are reviewed separately.

transition_receipt.message: The issue status was successfully changed.

entries.comment: Reviewed at wxnotepad 7ff2e5d. CheckWord deliberately exercises the pinned VectorISA calling convention: uint32_t storage is passed through the MSVC-compatible long* signature. The actual Linux _bittest/_bittestandset/_bittestandreset adapters in src/editor/platform/intrinsics_port.h never dereference that pointer as long; they memcpy exactly sizeof(uint32_t) into/out of a uint32_t object. The fixture checks all 32 bit positions, an adjacent guard word and a single uint32_t allocation, and passed at -O2 with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (LeakSanitizer disabled because this executor uses ptrace). The cast is the interoperability behavior under test, not aliasing through a long lvalue.

transition_receipt.message: The issue status was successfully changed.

entries.comment: Reviewed at wxnotepad 7ff2e5d and pinned Notepad4 89b8b36. Message::GetZoom returns ViewStyle::zoomLevel (int), constrained by SetZoom/ZoomIn/ZoomOut to MinZoomLevel=10 through MaxZoomLevel=500. GetDPI().y is int. Their intptr_t product has magnitude at most INT_MAX*500, below 2^40, so conversion to the supported double type preserves the integer exactly before the intended DPI scaling/rounding. No arbitrary 64-bit document position enters this conversion.

entries.comment: Reviewed at wxnotepad 7ff2e5d and pinned Notepad4 89b8b36. CanDiscardUntitledWhitespace receives the byte range of a short untitled document; the loop reads the returned character storage before any document mutation. Editor::WndProc(Message::GetRangePointer) returns AsInteger<sptr_t>(pdoc->RangePointer(...)); Document::RangePointer returns const char*, and sptr_t is intptr_t. entries.comment: Reviewed at wxnotepad 7ff2e5d and pinned Notepad4 89b8b36. SelectByMouse line 33 populates GDK's double-valued mouse coordinate using PointXFromPosition or PointYFromPosition plus half TextHeight. The pinned message handlers return int coordinates and ViewStyle::lineHeight is int; Send merely widens them to intptr_t for message transport. Even the sum of a signed 32-bit coordinate and half a signed 32-bit height is far below 2^53, so every possible transported coordinate is exactly representable as GDK gdouble. Document byte positions are only inputs to the coordinate lookup, not the values converted to double.

transition_receipt.message: The issue status was successfully changed.

entries.comment: Reviewed at wxnotepad 7ff2e5d. AfterPresentation/Preparation obtains a non-null wl_surface* from gdk_wayland_window_get_wl_surface for the owned test window and passes it to wl_proxy_get_id. Wayland protocol objects are wl_proxy objects behind opaque protocol-specific types; its official client API examples likewise cast a wl_surface* to struct wl_proxy*. entries.comment: Reviewed tests/measurement_threads.cpp:173 at 7ff2e5d1. CheckWorkers catches all worker-body exceptions into the slot indexed by that worker using current_exception. exception_transport_clarification: The S2738 dispositions concern capture and deferred propagation through std::exception_ptr. std::current_exception may copy the exception object; the cross-platform regression checks the propagated exception type and message. Historical submitted comments and receipts are retained verbatim.

entries.comment: This is the clipboard-peer shutdown diagnostic. The fixed "%s" format receives std::exception::what(); it must remain available on the supported GCC 13 build. The project selects gcc-13/g++-13 in .github/actions/dependencies/action.yml (lines 54 and 83). GCC's libstdc++ implementation table records P2093R14 formatted output/std::print as first supported in GCC 14.1 (https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/libstdc++/manual/status.html), also listed in the GCC 14 release notes (https://gcc.gnu.org/gcc-14/changes.html). C++23 language mode does not provide the missing GCC 13 library facility. Therefore this specific recommendation to replace fprintf with std::print is a toolchain-compatibility false positive; the supported std::format conversions in this PR are handled separately.

entries.comment: False positive caused by treating a lambda's separate function body as a nested exception handler in its caller. In tests/measurement_workers.h, the outer try encloses launch/construction of worker threads; every actual launcher constructs a std::jthread (the regression launcher can instead throw before construction). The lambda is the worker-thread entry function and its inner try/catch captures work(worker) failures into that worker's exception_ptr. A worker exception cannot propagate across the thread boundary into the caller's startup catch. After successful startup, workers are joined and captured failures are rethrown after the outer try/catch has ended. Thus these are distinct startup and worker execution exception boundaries, already separated by the callable function boundary; there is no ambiguous nesting of catches for the same exception path.

receipt.message: The issue status was successfully changed.

entries.comment: False positive under S2738's documented rethrow exception. This startup catch handles a failure after some std::jthreads have been created. It removes the participants that were never started from the barrier, then executes an explicit `throw;` at the end of the handler. Started jthreads are joined by their destructors during unwinding, while the barrier and failure slots are still alive. The catch does not convert an arbitrary startup failure into success or discard it. S2738 explicitly excludes catch handlers that rethrow the same exception with `throw;`; the cleanup statements before that rethrow do not change this classification.

receipt.message: The issue status was successfully changed.

entries.comment: False positive, verified against every call site at revision d641fc408137c7d9d0393b603c6068bc3b7c78f7. Typing has internal linkage in the anonymous namespace of tests/auto_completion_settings.cpp and is called only at lines 252, 257 and 277. All calls follow Require(requestedBit > 0 && requestedBit <= 256 && std::has_single_bit(static_cast<unsigned long>(requestedBit))) at lines 240-242. Require throws when false; the immutable int bit is created only after this check, preserving the validated value exactly. The tags/words branches return at lines 229/238 and never call Typing, including for their zero placeholder. Inside Typing, bit < 256 therefore admits only {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128}; countr_zero yields only 0..7, within the eight opening characters (nine array elements including NUL) and the closing-character table. The other valid value, 256, takes the line-comment branch without indexing these arrays. The reported index 32 is the countr_zero result for zero on 32-bit unsigned; zero cannot reach this path. Native Windows, X11 and Wayland runs all passed the fixture, including all nine valid bits and ten invalid mode/flag combinations.

receipt.message: The issue status was successfully changed.

entries.comment: Known analyzer false-positive pattern SONARPY-3154. This expression parses the owned Weston window geometry for the move-peer request: each str.split("=", 1) produces the key/value sequence consumed directly by dict(), with one split per line. It is not the redundant dict((k, v) for ...) pattern with separately available key and value expressions. SonarSource's own S7494 fixture explicitly labels dict(x.split("=") for x in update_str.split(",")) as "FP SONARPY-3154" (https://github.com/SonarSource/sonar-python/blob/9ae0129e3f7b41be37b3b128e4b6447b467c278a/python-checks/src/test/resources/checks/rewriteCollectionConstructorAsComprehension.py#L44-L49). Reintroducing {key: value for key, value in (line.split(...) for ...)} adds the copy-only comprehension correctly reported by S7500; duplicate splitting or extra binding loops would only complicate this parser. The current constructor preserves first-separator splitting, input order, last-duplicate-key behavior, and rejection of malformed pairs.

receipt.message: The issue status was successfully changed.
